newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines to speed up disclosure after crashes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines to speed up disclosure after crashes.

text.p: Seven major U.S. airines agreed to provide the State Department with passenger manifest information within three hours of international aviation accidents that involve U.S. citizens, the Air Transport Association said on Wednesday.
The State Department will then be able to more quickly determine next-of-kin information and provide it to the airline, the association said.

"The airlines have long sought to better coordinate their activities with the State Department," said ATA president Carol Hallett. "These new procedures will help us make that contact as quickly as possible and assist the State Department in fulfilling its responsibilities as well.'
The airlines involved in the pact agreed to participate with the State Department in each other's emergency training programs, ATA said.
The pact also outlined procedures for the exchange of personnel when airline accidents occur, allowing close coordination between command centers and the accident site.

The airlines participating in the pact include AMR Corp's American Airlines, Continental Airlines, Delta Air Lines Inc, Northwest Airlines, Trans World Airlines, UAL Corp's United and USAir Group Inc.
